blocks.text: Street performers on stilts in front of the cathedral in a square in Bogotá, Colombia
Bogotá: performers in bright costumes in the square in front of the cathedral

After breakfast, set out on a guided tour of Medellín.

The city began as a mining settlement in the 17th century. Today, Medellín is known as the city of eternal spring and orchids. It is Colombia’s second-largest city, where old churches and mansions sit alongside modern neighbourhoods.

You’ll see the Metropolitan Cathedral Basilica, described as South America’s largest brick church, and visit the Museum of Antioquia and the area known as ‘Botero City’. This large area includes a sculpture park with works by Fernando Botero, who was born in Medellín. There are also recreation areas, galleries and artists’ studios.

The tour also explores the city’s complex history. Medellín is known for its flowers, festivals, innovation and culture, and its past is closely tied to drug cartels and Pablo Escobar. Comuna 13, where the drug lord once hid, is now a popular area for visitors.

The final stop is El Castillo Museum, which houses a collection of decorative and applied arts. Built in 1930 in the Gothic style, it resembles a French castle. The house first belonged to Dr Uribe and was later bought by the philanthropist Diego Misas, who assembled an art collection there. It eventually became a museum and cultural centre.

Return to the hotel.
